action: Cursor asks users who installed or updated to Claude Code extension 2.1.312 or 2.1.313 on October 29 to follow its security notice (uninstalling alone may not be enough); it emailed team admins the specific keys to rotate.
attack: T1195.002 Supply Chain Compromise: Compromise Software Supply Chain
exec: Cursor says a supplier's exposed key led to tampered add-on copies that at most 5,000 users potentially received; it says it moved inference off Fireworks.
plain: Coding-tool maker Cursor says a key it gave supplier Fireworks AI was exposed and used to copy data, then malicious copies of a popular add-on were served for about 11 hours on October 29; at most 5,000 users potentially received them.

key_findings: An attacker used an access key Cursor had issued to Fireworks AI, which Fireworks exposed, to copy data from a read-only storage bucket.
The bucket held coding agent traces, mostly from 2025, from sessions not in Privacy Mode; under 0.01% of customers had API credentials exposed.
Credentials in those traces opened some SaaS tools, archived non-production repositories, limited support data and usage metrics.
On October 29 malicious copies of the Claude Code extension, versions 2.1.312 and 2.1.313, sat in the marketplace cache for about 11 hours; at most 5,000 users could have received them.
Cursor saw the last attacker activity on November 1 and moved all inference off Fireworks; Fireworks' own bulletin dates its first intrusion to August 3 to October 7.
recommendations: If you installed or updated to Claude Code extension 2.1.312 or 2.1.313 during the window, follow Cursor's October 30 security notice; uninstalling alone may not be enough.
Rotate any exposed keys; admins were sent lists of affected keys.
Fireworks customers: create new API keys, rotate third-party credentials named in your notice and review access logs for those credentials.

evidence.quote: At most 5,000 users who requested specific cached versions of the extension on October 29 potentially received the malicious build.
It was available for approximately 11 hours before we removed it.

summary: Cursor's November 13 update says an access key it had issued to Fireworks AI was exposed by that supplier and used to copy coding agent traces from a read-only bucket. Credentials found in the traces let the attacker reach select SaaS tools used by Cursor. On October 29 the attacker placed malicious Claude Code extension builds 2.1.312 and 2.1.313 in Cursor's marketplace cache for about 11 hours; at most 5,000 users potentially received them.
title: Cursor says exposed Fireworks AI key led to malicious Claude Code extension copies

validation.note: Cursor's own update (primary) states the core fact; Fireworks AI's bulletins and The Hacker News were also read. Fireworks' bulletins do not mention Cursor's key.

review.note: Stronger than the source ('reaching' 5,000 users, 'internal tools'), action advice (rotate keys Fireworks flagged not stated), unsupported ai-enabled tag; figures 11 hours/5,000 match Cursor
